title: The Fermi Paradox
summary:
Over lunch at Los Alamos in 1950, the physicist Enrico Fermi asked something like "Where is everybody?" There are hundreds of billions of stars in our galaxy, many far older than the Sun, and many with planets; even slow travellers could have crossed the galaxy many times over. Michael Hart argued in 1975 that, since no one has visited us, we are probably the only civilisation in the Galaxy. Others suggest that life is rare, that civilisations don't last, that they stay quiet, or that we are simply early.

Whether to call out is a newer argument. In 1974 the Arecibo telescope beamed a short message towards the star cluster M13; it will arrive in about 25,000 years. David Brin, writing about the "Great Silence" in 1983, asked whether others keep quiet for a reason. In 2015 a group of scientists signed a statement that no one should transmit on behalf of the whole Earth without a worldwide discussion first. Others answer that we have been leaking radio into space for a century already, and that saying hello is worth the risk.
